suggestions: Replace the multiplicative triple-product with an additive fusion of three independently smoothed, cross-sectionally ranked legs—Rank(Ma((close-open)/(high-low),10),40) + Rank(Zscore(Log(volume),20),40) + Rank((high-low)/Ma((high-low),20),40)—before a final long-window Rank(60). When direction, volume, and range expansion are multiplied, a single mean-reverting leg can flip the entire composite sign overnight; additive ranked components decay independently, producing a slower-moving conviction score that reduces day-to-day rank reversals and the validation RankIR collapse seen with the current structure.

Apply a persistence gate before scaling the directional leg: only pass (close-open)/(high-low) through when both Zscore(volume,10) > 0 and (high-low)/Ma((high-low),5) > 1 for at least 3 consecutive sessions (otherwise emit 0 or carry forward the prior gated value). The alpha currently treats isolated volume or range spikes as full conviction events; requiring simultaneous, sustained confirmation filters one-off microstructure and gap-driven outliers that dominate short-horizon noise and cause unstable cross-sectional ordering across market regimes.

Replace the outer Rank(20) with a two-stage cross-sectional memory: Rank(inner_composite, 60) followed by Ema(..., 10), and lengthen the range-expansion denominator to Ma((high-low), 20) instead of 5 days. A 20-day rank window forces daily wholesale reordering of names (turnover 1.76), while longer rank memory keeps relative ordering stable across weeks; the Ema layer dampens residual cross-sectional jumps without the heavy Ma+Corr+volatility-normalization stack that increased overfitting in prior children.
